# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document accompanies
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md) and
> expands the RFC’s phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> RFC-039’s main text is the sole authority for phase order and acceptance gates; this document is
> responsible only for decomposing the work to an executable granularity and registering conflicts
> that remain unadjudicated.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, corresponding one-to-one with RFC-039’s phase sequence                                   |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each able to form and archive a team independently |
| **Level 3** | 268         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                      |

**Numbering gaps (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP route
was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). All three have had no
corresponding entries since the WBS was established—the entire history of this document has zero
matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can verify this), and there
are no repository-wide references. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion): that phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8’s numbering aligns with its
phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered here**: Task decomposition, dependency relationships, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered here**: The design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale for phase
ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: Every newly registered level-2/level-3 row
**must contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P to which it truly belongs, which may differ
from its current section) and “**Blocks the mainline**”; `pending scheduling` is no longer the
default state, and an unmarked task is considered **not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique
throughout the document** (cross-track tasks use a track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not
occupy an `N.x` number).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: Checked rows contain only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when present)—on
one line: `- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining Pattern-Matching Completion** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do
not record the fix, the criterion chain, gate values, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a
dashboard, not a process chronicle. **Do not record adjudication labels or restate conclusions**:
“User adjudication A/B/C,” “Option A,” “Option B,” and “The final implementation is…” must not
appear in this table—the dashboard answers only “Is it complete?” Consult the commit message and
RFC-039’s adjudication register for decisions and outcomes.

**Short hashes are authoritative only after pushing**: A closure row records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push is complete; the order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure row** (see “Take the commit number after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure commit itself does not carry a
number—self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains numbers only**: The level-1/2/3 counts under “Positioning and Scope”
contain current values only; increment/decrement history (`+1 = …`) does not belong in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “implementation points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Resolution                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC defines P5 (checker splitting) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents contains a section describing how to perform the split; a single `annotations.rs` line appeared in the directory tree of `01-routing.md`, the only mention in the entire batch                                                   | The P5 steps are supplied here (see below)                                                                                                     |
| G2  | **The three `include!` conversions have inconsistent ownership and no implementation**. RFC places them in P4; `02`’s cross-reference assigns them to itself; S7 of `06` also lists them. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) **does not include `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                           | The implementation steps belong to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); references in RFC and 06 now point here                    |
| G3  | **Three coexisting CI-script inventories**. `RFC` lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists 4 different checks; `04` also listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts but no unified inventory**; `check-obligations.py` has dual ownership in P4 and P9 | See §P9 of this document for the unified inventory (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to this table       |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life or death of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines requiring revival,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                   | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registered as C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                   |
| G5  | **Conflicting description of the L2 objective**: RFC and this directory’s index formerly said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | This has converged on **a declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Reason for adding P0**: The three prohibitions—no fabrication, no endless padding, and no patching
when a refactor is required—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established before
work begins; otherwise, when P1 revives tests, it will already be adding `mod` declarations to
`tests/mod.rs`, which is precisely what caused the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Approach)

Source: Vulnerability-fix half of §Implementation Point S3 in [02](02-stage-contract.md) ＋
**2026-10-07 silent-discard-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, adjudicated 2026-10-11)**: If this track or a subsequent phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack exhaustion, or silently
> returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactoring**, but all four
> requirements must be met: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and actually
> fail); ② the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled successfully and
> ran correctly” must not change (they must not begin failing, and their existing diagnostic
> codes/prose/exit codes must not be removed or modified); ③ registration in the same commit (this
> row must identify the error type + include a revision note for the phase + the PR must contain the
> required “Error Type” line); ④ baseline regeneration and manual diff review in the same commit.
> **D user-visible semantics / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes still require
> prior adjudication.** See [07 §Semantic-Correction Routing Criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for
> the expanded criteria and A–F allowlist; **the “default super-refactor followed by retrospective
> registration” approach is not adopted** (the rationale is RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion,
> there is no way to distinguish a fix from a regression, and it conflicts with both “C5′ does not
> exist” and “no relaxation whatsoever”).

The investigation disproves the premise that it “can be fixed in passing as class C”: the probe matrix measures that heterogeneous container Eq shapes (`[1,2]==(1,2)` / `[1]==["x"]` / `[1]==[2.5]` / `(1,2)==(1,"x")`) compile successfully and **run successfully, printing false**—compile-time rejection would change the observable behavior of programs that previously ran successfully ⇒ D59 **class D**, so it does not satisfy the conditions for an incidental fix; heterogeneous scalar / static-Void / heterogeneous Dict comparisons produce runtime E6007 (the old behavior was not successful, so they may be fixed incidentally, but this is not an independent adjudication point); it was also observed that same-typed Dict==Dict produces runtime E6007 (no comparison arm for Handle), which is recorded without adjudication. The sole adjudication point = whether heterogeneous container Eq should be rejected at compile time (Option A: compile-time rejection, with full alignment to the discipline that both sides of an ordering comparison have the same type (the criterion body = the infer_binary comparison arm)—recommended; Option B: retain runtime false and use the design process); all four parts of the complete adjudication package are in the comments of issue [#549](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/549). **Acceptance**: The vulnerability criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fixes must
turn them red again**. **Risk**: The new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 Acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must first have red criteria (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 requires manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 follow C2/C3 and gate 9.2 in P9. **Risk**: The new
diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus-differential baseline
and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 does not need to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**; the
> remainder of P2 (2.1 IR verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differentials and performance
> baseline) can proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the correctness vulnerability (`Sorted(3)`
> silently passing) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3
> (panic-to-diagnostic conversion) has no prerequisite and can land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactoring itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by
an ordering constraint**; it is separate from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust’s
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why the whole track must precede P4**: RFC-029g’s deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite
surfaces of all four refactoring phases. Reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| 029g Deletion Surface                                               | File                                                                                                               | Rewritten by Which Phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `KwPub` and its syntax branches                                     | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexical convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 splitting `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                                |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory renaming (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                             |
| The `pub` branches of `auto_bind_to_type` and `collect_exports`     | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!` → real `mod` and checker splitting are **pure moves**, so the `pub` branches will be moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                                                    |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (slimming down `check_project`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| The `Public` modifier in `semantic_tokens`                          | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `is_pub` ignoring bindings in `ir_gen`                              | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (SSA-ification of `ir_gen.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase changes them directly, but **P6’s hard acceptance criterion requires zero difference in `src/std/`** (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; directly driven tests under `tests/` are exempt as described in P6’s hard-acceptance section)—they can only land before P6 |

**Incidental benefit**: 029g deletes the dead `env.exports` table (filled by the producer and never
consumed repository-wide) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors → one fewer “produced but
never consumed” field in P4’s 4.3 obligation ledger.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: Each of the two behavioral changes must land a red criterion before code
   changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced top-level
   bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously `pub` items were absolutely exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: When deleting the `exempt_pub` cases in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixtures, equivalent new cases must
   replace them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: Diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) → the
   corpus-differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG are updated in
   the same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero difference, and any nonzero difference
   requires an explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: The entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` must all be green.

**Ordering**: It overlaps with 3.4 files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) → the two must be serial
and cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; the implementer chooses which to start based on available context.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: The incorporation of this section (P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) and RFC-039’s D56 were included in `97071c81b` during a parallel-stream
> cleanup of the workspace—the commit message records “3.4 supplementary registration + D57/D58
> adjudication filing” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten; it is registered
> in place according to the existing style (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing note) as
> evidence for later bisecting.

|                                                   | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method called with **named arguments** loses its formal-parameter-name table (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closure round): calling a cross-unit (registry-injected) method with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named-argument calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` uses `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: class C** (old behavior unsuccessful: named arguments are silently dropped, followed by runtime failure or a silent wrong value). **Scope (final form after two rounds of narrowing on 2026-11-26—only three additions; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—obtain declaration-time formal-parameter names from the sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads`, using the definition unit’s qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` (the candidate ↔ mixed IR name ↔ formal-parameter-name vectors are in the same order as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses `method_dispatch_name`’s qualified name to find the name table rather than two separate bare names. These two sites fix only **bare-name imports** (`local == target`) for cross-unit methods: the candidate-injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (`local != target` is skipped), so named arguments for alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**class C (independent of the original bug): eliminate “the same input, multiple results” caused by HashMap iteration order**, not a fix of the original bug; criterion = same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is allowed for the same method key; removing the ascending merge produces two results). **Criterion (red before green)**: two driver-level tests in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (bare import with a single candidate 6.0 / two candidates selected by name 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; file header marked as a failure-history gate); unit tests in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (empty-name-table guard for `method_param_info` ⇒ None, positive control returns the non-empty table unchanged); unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the determinism criterion above). Project fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted along with the alias surface’s retirement); the corpus-differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (the intermediate state had included `alias-overload`); **relative to pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 basic fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` never entered the final history). The line-count change is an unavoidable consequence of fixtures entering and leaving (after `corpus_probe` regeneration, it matches the committed baseline byte for byte), **not lost coverage**. **Known gaps (each named explicitly; old behavior = silently ignored or silently discarded; D60② class A)**: closure-value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested-function declaration / built-in container constructors other than `len` named arguments / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two points are corrected according to P0’s measured semantics**: ① **static-function shapes** (both same-unit and cross-unit, definition form and binding form) are **entirely unavailable today**—same-unit `check` reports E3006, cross-unit definition-form `run` reports E6007, and cross-unit binding-form `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code, unrelated to named arguments, and this is not “named arguments being silently discarded”; ② **RFC-004 cross-unit positional arguments also fail** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006), because the dispatch name is not in the merged function table; this too is unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 class A incidental fix: the old E6007/E1014 behavior was unsuccessful, so no previously successful program becomes a failure)**: ① **alias-imported named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). These previously produced, respectively, runtime E6007 silently dropping arguments and compile-time `E1014 (available: )` false rejections; all now enter the correct slot by declaration-time formal-parameter name (value assertion 6.0; criterion `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with the red state recorded in the file-header failure-history gate of `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`). the remaining one is function-body-level / cross-scope imports merged globally by unit (shared import table)—this shape does not work in the first place (existing defect: check passes, run reports E6006), was not introduced by this batch, and remains unfixed. **Deletions in this round (relative to the six rounds before 4.9.9)**: candidate-provider priority, candidate-signature comparison, owner/compatibility inference, the `frontend::module::import_face` shared-provider table, the IR-side “cannot obtain the name table ⇒ E1014” fallback, and the **E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution points**—the latter rejects mixed/alias-only shapes that ran on the parent commit (class D), and was withdrawn by the 2026-11-26 decision; |                                                   | 4.9.10 Cross-unit method identity is undefined (registered 2026-11-25; structural problem confirmed during 4.9.9 implementation): the method-candidate key `{Type}.{method}` does not include module qualification, so for same-named types in different modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`driver::arms::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck’s formal-parameter-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—each guess the provider by name, and changing any one of them moves the “silent wrong value” elsewhere. **Root-cause solution**: upgrade type identity to **module-qualified identity** (`{module}.{Type}`), and change the method-candidate key accordingly to `{module}.{Type}.{method}`; one resolver produces it, and three consumers only read it. This requires changing the shape of the `overload_resolutions` key and the mixed names, making it D59 **class D** (requiring adjudication). **Disposition in this round (after two rounds of narrowing following 4.9.9)**: 4.9.9 **introduces no new rejection**—the class-D rejection list from the previous six rounds (all named arguments ⇒ E1014 / conflicting shapes with positional arguments ⇒ E1107 / E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution points) is deleted together with the mechanism and all invalidated; **import shapes and positional arguments** for mixed / alias-only / conflicting shapes that ran on the parent commit are restored to working order. **Residual surface (after this round closes)**: ① function-body-level / cross-scope imports merged globally by unit (shared import table), a shape that does not work in the first place (check passes, run reports E6006); ② named arguments are still silently ignored or discarded in certain shapes (D60② class A): **static-function shapes** (same-unit `check` E3006; cross-unit definition-form `run` E6007; cross-unit binding-form `run` E6006—positional and named arguments produce the same code, unrelated to named arguments), **RFC-004 cross-unit** (positional arguments also report E6006), **closure-value binding**, **block-body function declaration**, and **built-in container constructors other than `len`** (shapes such as `size`: the named argument is ignored and `length` is 0, producing runtime E6005; the `len` shape is normal). **Three items closed in this round**: ① method-candidate keys / method keys changed to module-qualified `{module}.{Type}.{method}` (L0’s `DefPath` dual representation + S2a’s table key and single-point resolution; all three consumers named at registration—`visible_method_overloads`, formal-parameter-name lookup `method_param_info`, and `method_dispatch_name`—have been deleted); ② the unit’s own same-named type + alias import (two coexisting same-named definition-side identities); ③ named arguments for alias imports / the namespace arm / inferred receivers (three shapes turn green; see the 4.9.9 paragraph). **L3 type-identity residuals (migration surface, unfixed; already red at L0 and not a regression in this round)**: ① the type name itself is still not module-qualified—the static type name in `MonoType` is the **definition-side bare name**, so same-named types in different units still cannot be distinguished at the type layer and can only be worked around using the import surface + binding identity; ② `VarInfo::type_identity` covers only the **local-binding** registration point (written annotation / constructor-written path), while **formal parameters, pattern bindings, closure parameters, and `for` variables** are not registered—at these positions, the receiver can still be resolved only by static type name (`set_type_identity` has only one call site repository-wide). **Status**: closed 2026-11-29. L0 / S1 / S2a / S2b and L3 (type-representation-layer identity, D64) have all been implemented—a single identity encoding (`types/identity.rs` is the sole home of `DefPath`/`DefId`/`DefKind`/`TypePath`/`Nominal`; `module::symbol` has zero re-exports; `from_def_path` enforces an empty owner, zero disambiguation, and legal bare names); five nominal surfaces hold `Nominal`; `rebind_nominal_refs`/`qualify_deferred_method`/`import_type_rebinds` are fully removed; `env.types` / sum types / generic / record models / the two lower tables are queryable by identity (`TypeEnvironment::add_type` writes both “identity → first written name” and “written name → identity” tables in one write, with a unique writer); display and hashing still use bare names (`Debug`/`Display`/`type_name`/`to_type_id`/vtable keys have zero difference). Commits: `7ce52fae3` (L3-0 identity descent), `6223d6d59` (L3-1a five-surface `Nominal` replacement), conversion funnel and S1/S2/S3 prerequisite commits, `65861410f` (identity propagated through production and consumption), `cd9cded27` (lower tables + §2.5 sites), `28fad48c2`, `6c5a3d673` (written-name → identity forward table + dual keys), `3efe68ec0` (census semantics). path of `collect_used_in_type` must not change)

- [x] **5.2 Extract `refinement`** (2 level-3 tasks)
- [x] **5.3 Extract `annotations`** (2 level-3 tasks)

| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 5.1 `include!` → real `mod` | 5.1.1 Replace the `include!` at the end of `checker.rs` with a real `mod` declaration (do not hard-code line anchors; at the time of measurement it was the final line)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | P4 complete  | C1 zero-diff; `semantic_tokens.rs` gains module identity                                                                                        |
|                             | 5.1.2 Add `use super::*` or import items individually (`include!` implicitly inherited the scope in the old form)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | 5.1.1        | `cargo build` is green                                                                                                                          |
| 5.2 Extract `refinement`    | 5.2.1 Move out the refinement blocks (three non-contiguous sections of the original `checker.rs`; now one file, `checker/refinement.rs`, containing `ReturnRefinement` / `RefinedWalkCtx`), leaving the public surface and six cross-boundary shared items in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | 5.1.1        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                    |
|                             | 5.2.2 Consolidate the refinement entry point into “`&self` + return diagnostics,” **without leaving the impl**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer uses `&mut self` to write to the error channel implicitly; the diagnostic set is returned upward, and the sole write point is in the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Rationale for remaining in the impl**: the only field used by this family is `self.env` (technically, leaving the impl is feasible), but converting both the entry point and traversal to free functions would move all these call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 producers (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 producers + 1 test, and it would create a reverse dependency from the “retained surface (signature collection)” to refinement—the opposite of the coupling this step is intended to eliminate | 5.2.1        | —                                                                                                                                               |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move out the 10-item annotation-validation family (now one file, `checker/annotations.rs`; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a free function within the family)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | 5.2.2        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                    |
|                             | 5.3.2 **`collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) remains `pub(crate)` and under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 was measured **not to migrate it** ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Retained constraint**: if it is moved with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 5.3.1        | **Zero caller changes** is the hard acceptance criterion for this step: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; 5.3 was
measured **not to migrate it**, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of only 200–400 lines—this adds
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) will be split only after the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62’s end state is a **unified term world**—type positions and value positions share
> one set of compile-time terms. A strength declaration produces a quantifier reading `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`;
> `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual-argument view and the
> implementation-head binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> determination** (the same after normalizing both sides; it does not bind type variables); evidence
> is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value environment/single-value
> pinning/Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (it holds for closed and
> open/recursive terms); Σ construction points **reuse** the same evidence interface and do not
> establish another one. **The completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that a subphase name
> has run.**

> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and completed; F4 decision → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may proceed in parallel but require

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 decision (adjudicated as A, 2026-11-16; measured)**: The old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that an open term’s `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request
> is created, and the representation `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold `k-1`. **The
> decision changes to two orthogonal decisions plus one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: do not
> specialize); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1: recovering the second field from IR breaks the
> single representation/evaluator, C-2: the second field cannot be recovered from IR, C-3 = A);
> **F4-T termination** (naive firing pushes the recursion chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005;
> T-a: condition on the instance within the firing / T-b: bounded firing + fallback to the original
> at the boundary / T-c: termination layer or change the specification). **Measure first, then
> adjudicate; before measurement, do not treat “A is implementable” as a conclusion.** **User
> (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task; do
> not claim that I4 is fully implemented.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet documented)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that
> “a decision point first follows unification; after unified failure, it may use equality, but it
> must first roll back the partial bindings produced by the unification attempt.” The implementation
> must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new `decide` layer;
> may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (have no unbound variables); what are the
> snapshot/restoration boundaries and costs; and do unify and defeq share one budget or have
> separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for subtyping/Any/Never;
> defeq only determines equivalence and does not take over subtyping, and bidirectional subtyping
> must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol and production call
> graph before writing code**; 6.9.3c’s wiring contract was wasted on two rounds because it assumed
> `can_assign` was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: Every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ error-code-generator idempotence (if an emission point/code table changes); ④
> behavioral changes classified under D59 and red before green. **Wiring tasks additionally
> require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how many paths, which
> path is reachable); unit-test reachability must not be passed off as user reachability; rollback
> and budget require measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537 (class D, silent discard of
> proof-function formal-parameter refinement; do not fix before adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must
> not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; a C-phase boundary; if not closed, 6.9.4 covers
> only module-internal cases), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 closed on
> 2026-11-14: orchestration-layer 64MB large-stack thread + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 +
> E0019, see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall; **closed**—three synchronized changes on
> 2026-11-16: `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover
> `Call`/`TailCall` through the single rewritten-call-target point, with the init section and
> function body sharing one site-rewriting implementation; red→green + three mutations), #542
> (orphaned shared layer; **landed (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two entry-point
> connections + removal of the C2c temporary avoidance; red→green, 402/402, function-table
> attribution and deviations), #552 (importing multi-parameter predicates for proof execution; a
> 6.9.5-neighbor case, separate). **Ownership pending adjudication**: the four open-constraint
> tripwires of `rfc027_refined_transparency` (`Eq(N, n)`) do not belong to 6.9.4’s constant-equality
> bridge; decide whether they remain in 6.9.4’s outOfScope or move to 6.9.1/E4018’s proof-function
> surface.

> **Non-claims/boundaries**: This item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim that Π/Σ are fully implemented; 6.9.4 covers only constant
> equalities and does not fulfill the `Eq(N,n)` tripwire, and the second value position of `f(y)(y)`
> is not in this item; witness erasure ≠ Runtime check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5
> only cover shapes that do not depend on proof-function formal-parameter refinement; if #539 is not
> fixed, 6.9.4 only covers module-internal cases; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 has landed
> (2026-11-19); 2.1.4’s inner-isolation red state was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was
> rewritten by slot identity during 2.1.4 closure) ⇒ all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a
> gate are removed.

**Hard acceptance** (**semantics revised 2026-10-27, following decision ② of 2026-10-26**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Directly driven test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive modified code,
such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be changed when mechanically required by the change,
but each **file / line count / reason** must be registered; **tests must not be deleted and
assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new
diagnostic codes + baseline updates), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round with separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: The original semantics (decision ② of 2026-10-26) was written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-difference requirement to all of
> `tests/`; the revised semantics **changes only directly driven test files from “zero difference”
> to “changeable but with file / line count / reason registered”**, while the **zero-difference
> requirement for the corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and
> standard library (`src/std/`) remains unchanged**. First application = 6.1.2: only
> `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed **3 lines** (2 `assert_format_eq` instances,
> `i64`→`Int64`, plus 1 comment line), reason = the expected type name in the assertion must be
> synchronized when the changed spelling requires it; no tests were deleted and no assertions were
> weakened. See “P6 6.1 Name Normalization Closure.”

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (decision 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to **2.3.2 +
> 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The remainder of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differentials and performance baseline) can proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the correctness vulnerability must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every P1 action (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baselines                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must **first be written as red** (2.4.1/2.4.3), and the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to be frozen into the phase table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g’s (#399) deletion surface overlaps the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` conversion and checker split modify the same files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same files must be separated, otherwise regressions cannot be located by bisection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | Type representations must converge first, or the new IR will grow into a third representation; **the P7 gate = the A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completion of 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface but must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but must not consume the undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count can reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                        | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by the RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | The file sets are disjoint: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                    |
| B                                            | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| C                                            | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three criterion layers are independent                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| D                                            | 4.4 (proof-layer completion) ∥ the entire P6 line                                  | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                             |
| E                                            | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All become mutually independent after 4.1                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| F                                            | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced by P0 can be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| G                                            | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | The file sets are disjoint (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `src/docs/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub`s under `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pair overlaps) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same file batch); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s `pub` deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serial).

**New internal documentation constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the P7 prerequisite pure-move batch), and 7b’s `Phi` arm must
precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was required”; only
  D0–D4’s review checklist can do so.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative inventory of CI scripts**—the three coexisting inventories caused
  by original gap G3 could not be closed. This table merges them: each of the 10 active scripts is
  owned by one phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), and report-only status and
  hard-transition timing are explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to be done after the
  refactoring”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Leaving it until after the refactoring means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating 7e’s `2315`/`2341` and S4’s
  RFC status correction.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the available revert granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as hard acceptance**—the split must be independently
  revertable.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing the exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the fixed defects
  must not be rolled back” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: Every commit fixing an 1.3.x defect must reference the repaired test name and defect
  description in its commit message as evidence for later bisection.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: Split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two exclusive
  commits according to DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse**—approximately 89 reference renames, and a missed rename **silently changes
  associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34’s opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, and the deletion
  action landed in P10 S6.1 (6753bbe).
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally intended as “independent issues”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: `2341` was incorporated as 7e.3; `2315` was reviewed on 2026-11-28 and
  found to be an audit false positive (the field has no producer, and the language layer has no
  throw/try/catch), so 7e.2 was cancelled and the exception residue was deleted by P10 S6.1
  (6753bbe).
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  Incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode-gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: Incorporated
  into the build-time gate task in P10 S6.2 and landed (a2e570c).

> (D1–D50).** This document contains no remaining pending items. The one-to-one mapping is as
> follows:

| Original ID | Issue                                                                               | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1          | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                           | **Revive** (P1’s prerequisite is revival with real assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                                                             |
| C2          | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs table-driven implementation                          | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + a single declarative precedence table + cross-checking of two `BinOp` implementations from the same source (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn), see P8 8.3 |
| C3          | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification                   | **S1 is classified under C6** (revival does not require equivalence criteria, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                        |
| C4          | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` allowlist                                        | **No allowlist**; the difference set must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                          |
| C5          | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4’s 4.2.7 has already made this a mandatory verification item**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                                        |
| C6          | The wasm-playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                                 | **Merge the wasm-path vulnerability fix into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                           |
| C7          | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Assign to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                                                                        |
| C8          | Correction of `upvalue_count` and the `.42` version number                          | **Fix + change `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`), see D17                                                       |
